content.value_statement: Whole slide images are large and hard to prepare for tile analysis. This skill guides histolab workflows for masks, tiling, filters, and visual review.
actual_capabilities: Load and inspect whole slide images with dimensions, pyramid levels, thumbnails, and metadata.
Configure RandomTiler, GridTiler, and ScoreTiler workflows for different sampling needs.
Create tissue masks with TissueMask, BiggestTissueBoxMask, and custom BinaryMask approaches.
Build preprocessing pipelines with histolab image and morphological filters.
Preview masks and tile locations before extraction for quality control.
Troubleshoot common tile, tissue threshold, and performance problems.
limitations: It does not make clinical diagnoses or replace pathology review.
It assumes histolab, OpenSlide dependencies, and local slide files are available.
Very large WSI collections may need batching, storage planning, and memory limits.
Advanced spatial proteomics or multiplexed imaging workflows are better served by specialized tools.

use_cases.title: Prepare training tiles
use_cases.description: A machine learning engineer creates consistent 512 pixel image tiles from H&E slides for model training.

use_cases.title: Inspect tissue coverage
use_cases.description: A pathology researcher previews masks and tile locations before committing compute time to extraction.

use_cases.title: Standardize preprocessing
use_cases.description: An image analysis specialist builds repeatable filter pipelines for tissue detection, artifact removal, and quality review.

prompt_templates.title: Load and inspect a slide
prompt_templates.prompt: Show me a basic histolab workflow to load one SVS slide, inspect dimensions, save a thumbnail, and list useful metadata.

prompt_templates.title: Extract random training tiles
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me configure RandomTiler for 100 H&E tiles at 512 by 512 pixels. Include preview, seed, tissue threshold, and output review steps.

prompt_templates.title: Build a custom tissue mask
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a histolab TissueMask filter pipeline for H&E slides with pen marks. Include grayscale conversion, thresholding, morphology, preview, and validation checks.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a multi-slide tiling pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a multi-slide histolab workflow for consistent tile extraction across a cohort. Cover directory structure, pyramid level choice, reports, and quality control.

output_examples.input: I need training tiles from one H&E slide.
output: Recommended plan: load the slide, save a thumbnail, preview a tissue mask, then extract random 512 pixel tiles.
Set a fixed seed and tissue threshold so tile selection is repeatable.
Review a small tile preview before processing the full slide.
Lower small object removal thresholds and reduce erosion or opening strength.
Compare the mask against a thumbnail before extracting tiles.
Test changes on several slides with different stain quality.

output_examples.input: I need complete tissue coverage for spatial analysis.
output: Use GridTiler with no overlap for a complete baseline grid.
Choose a pyramid level that matches the required resolution and processing budget.
Save reports so tile positions remain traceable.

best_practices: Preview masks and tile positions before every large extraction run.
Use consistent pyramid levels and tile sizes across comparable slides.
Start with small batches to validate thresholds, output paths, and storage needs.
anti_patterns: Extracting thousands of tiles before checking tissue masks.
Mixing pyramid levels across slides without recording the difference.
Using one tissue threshold for every stain quality without validation.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps plan histolab workflows for WSI loading, tissue masks, tile extraction, filters, and visualization.

faq.question: Does it install histolab automatically?
faq.answer: No. It explains commands and workflows, but users control installation and execution.

faq.question: Which tiler should I choose?
faq.answer: Use RandomTiler for sampling, GridTiler for coverage, and ScoreTiler for quality driven selection.

faq.question: Can it support deep learning datasets?
faq.answer: Yes. It helps prepare image tiles and reports that can feed common training pipelines.

faq.question: Does it diagnose pathology images?
faq.answer: No. It supports preprocessing and quality review, not clinical interpretation.

faq.question: What inputs do I need?
faq.answer: You need local whole slide images, a configured histolab environment, and an output directory.
